Sorcerous Sundries is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3.
“
As luck would have it, we'll soon find ourselves near one of the finest book collections this side of Candlekeep - Sorcerous Sundries. <...> Their collection of rare tomes is unparallelled.
„
— Gale, after the first time seeing the Crown of Karsus

Overview

Sorcerous Sundries is a well-known store in Baldur's Gate, trading in various magical goods: elixirs and potions, spell scrolls, books, as well as weapons, armour and accessories.

Sorcerous Sundries is a large circular building with a dome made of elaborate multi-coloured stained glass. It is located in the heart of the Heapside district of the city. The only entrance to it is at X: -20 Y: -64, from a vast plaza lined up with Bonecloak's Apothecary, Central Watch Tower, and the Stormshore Armoury clinging to the Lower City Central Wall.

The party can visit its ground and first floors, and also its elaborate vault. Also, from the Sorcerous Sundries the party can travel to the Ramazith's Tower, towering above the Upper City of Baldur's Gate.

Building layout

Ground floor

After the shop's entrance is a large open area serving as main hall.

In the center of the room is a counter where a shopkeeper trades in scrolls, potions, and equipment. Depending on the party's prior decisions in various quests, this can be either  Lorroakan's Projection,  Rolan, or  Rolan's Projection. A  Potion of Sleep is on the counter.

Rolan is at the counter if he survived the events of Act One and Two. If the party speak to him, he reacts according to their prior actions (notably how he was spoken with in the Emerald Grove, and whether they saved his siblings from the Moonrise Towers Prison). The interacting party member can also observe that Rolan has been beaten recently, and ask him about it, rolling a passive  DC 10 Insight Check.[1]

The stairs to the both sides from the counter lead up to the first floor (see below).

The main trade hall encircles the counter, forming an inner an an outer lines of lesser counters, small tables, bookcases, and display cases. The hall is guarded by four Animated Armours. Various magical and alchemical items are here on display. Some of them are free to take, while most others are red-outlined (looting these is considered a crime). More notable items are as follows (going clockwise from the entrance):

  • At X: -1 Y: -64 on a counter are the  Coldbrim Hat, an  Elixir of Cold Resistance, the  Gold Wyrmling Staff, and  Winter's Clutches, as well as two Uncommon spell scrolls.
  • At X: 4 Y: -100 on a small table are a  Topaz and a  Sapphire.
  • At X: -18 Y: -90 on a small table is a  Potion of Speed and a  Potion of Mind Reading.
  • At X: -9 Y: -92 on the alchemy counter is a  Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen. On a table across from it is an  Elixir of Barkskin.
  • At X: -18 Y: -75 on a small table are two Uncommon scrolls. In a round bookshelf nearby is a  Potion of Invisibility.
  • A certain amount of common herbal alchemical ingredients such as  Weavemoss,  Mugwort and  Autumncroci can be freely looted from the counters.

The shop entertains its clients with various showpieces of magical nature. At X: -3 Y: -71 are tamed  lava and  water elementals. Also, the shop continuously casts the  Find Familiar spell, summoning random lesser conjured animals (a cat, a crab, a frog, a rat, or a spider) every three turns.

Several clients wander around shopping or simply gawking at the curios on display. Apart from the main counter, the two other shop staff are the necromancer  Cordrane the Recent, who sells zombies as home helpers and personal guards, and  Tolna Tome-Monger, the head of the shop's Literature Department.

Tolna Tome-Monger

Tolna Tome-Monger is at her counter at X: 8 Y: -92. She sells various books and Very rare spell scrolls.[2] If spoken with, Tolna can inform the party about the most rare ancient magical books owned by the Sorcerous Sundries, including the  The Annals of Karsus, the  The Tharchiate Codex, and two others which are never mentioned elsewhere in the game. She refuses to show these items, let alone sell them, but nevertheless can shed some light on their authors and themes.

If  Gale is in the party, and the interacting character asks Tolna about the "The Annals of Karsus", Gale chimes in, drawing the player character's attention to the book.

Tolna tells the party that these books are stored in the Sorcerous Vault. If the interacting party member passes an ability check ( DC 18 Deception Check,  DC 18 Persuasion Check,[3] or  DC 16 Intimidation Check), she tells them the vault can be entered through her office. She carries the  key to the office.

Under Tolna's counter lies the note labelled  The Path to Elminster, which can help the party navigate their way to unlock the "Elminster" section of the Sorcerous Vault (see the page about this).

Most books from Tolna's stock, particularly from the Magic Schools and The Apprentice's Companion series, can be taken for free from the non-restricted bookcases around the main trade hall.

First floor

Two stairs on the ground level lead up to the first floor, which consists of two rooms and the long stairs-landing between them. It is guarded by two more Animated Armours.

Upon entering for the first time the party encounter  Lorroakan's Projection at X: 14 Y: -72. It prompts a dialogue and informs them that the wizard  Lorroakan awaits first-hand information about the Nightsong only, and for those who have it, "knowledge will determine their path forward". Next, four portals open, each accompanied by a plaque giving a different explanation of what the  Nightsong might be. The only correct one is the pale blue portal at X: 13 Y: -83,[4] which transports the party to Ramazith's Tower, home and study of Lorroakan. The three others  down and eject from the building whomever attempts to enter.

The two rooms at each side of the landing are locked and red-outlined, each requires a  DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. Casting  Greater Invisibility or  Fog Cloud is helpful for sneaking undetected into any of the rooms (the door can be shut behind the party to avoid the Animated Armour noticing anything is amiss).

At X: -3 Y: -97 is a small bedroom with no signs of whom it might belong to. Little inside is of note, save for the note labelled  The Path to Karsus on the desk. It describes the way to navigate through the Sorcerous Vault to unlock the "Karsus" section.

The entrance to Tolna Tome-Monger's office is at X: 12 Y: -79. Apart from lockpicking, it can be opened with  Tolna's key. On the notice board here a  note concerning a djinni lamp is pinned, and on the desk is the  Sorcerous Sundries Basement Chest Key.

At X: 17 Y: -73 is a half-round bookcase containing another  Sorcerous Sundries Basement Chest Key. Interacting with the  Clasped Book (Sorcerous Sundries Office) in the bookcase opens a portal to the vault. Once used, the book cannot be interacted with anymore; the portal does not close.[5]

Despite its actual functioning similar to a button or a lever, this book can be destroyed like any other book in the game. Destroying it deprives the party of one of the ways to access the Sorcerous Vault.

Sorcerous Vault

Main article: Sorcerous Vault

The vault can be accessed in two ways: either through the aforementioned portal in Tolna's office, or from the lower level of the Ramazith's Tower.

Inside, the party can find all the books Tolna Tome-Monger mentions, including the Annals of Karsus, as well as numerous magical items, Very rare scrolls (some of which are in a single copy throughout the game), and Valuables. They can also find the djinni lamp mentioned in the note in Tolna's office, and progress several quests, including Gale's personal quest (both as companion and origin).

Involvement and companion interactions

The Sorcerous Sundries is a location where several major quests can be progressed.

  • The magical shop is the place where  Gale hopes to find information on the  Crown of Karsus. The book he needs to read is called "The Annals of Karsus" and is hidden in the restricted vault, for it contains knowledge possibly dangerous for both the reader and those around them. Convincing Tolna Tome-Monger to reveal where the book is kept progresses Gale's personal quest (either companion or origin).
  • The same mechanism works for the ⁠Unlock the Ancient Tome quest, save for the book in question. To progress this quest, the party must find and read "The Tharchiate Codex", which is also kept in the magic store's vault. The party may know about the way to progress this quest depending on whether they have read the  Necromancy of Thay and bargained with  Mystic Carrion at Philgrave's Mansion beforehand. Regardless, if the party asks Tolna Tome-Monger about the Codex, she mentions the Necromancy of Thay, and the quest is updated.
  • The Sorcerous Sundries is owned by the wizard Lorroakan, who announced far and wide a contract to ⁠Find the Nightsong. Talking to Aradin, to Rolan, and to Lorroakan himself reveal that Lorroakan became obsessed with finding the Nightsong and binding her to gain her immortality. However, he did not tell any of the adventurers who signed up for the task any details either about the true nature of the requested "item" or about "its" exact location.[6]

Outside

  • If  Aradin survived the events of Act One, he can be found at the entrance to the Sorcerous Sundries, trying to meet Lorroakan in person. However, the guard  Klank blocks him. If the party speak to Aradin, he recognizes them. If he also was convinced to yield  Lorroakan's contract on retrieving Nightsong, Aradin will try to find out whether the party succeeded in finding it. The party can pass various ability checks to discourage or deceive him, or invite Aradin to their camp to kidnap Dame Aylin.
Choosing the latter option is considered an oathbreaking action for Paladins of any Oath subclass.[verify]
  • In the middle of the plaza is a fountain. Near it, a group of wizards:  Astoundo the Greater,  Astoundo the Lesser, and  Salamander perform magic shows, casting various common cantrips and conjuring lesser familiars. A small crowd of onlookers, including several children, watch the show. At the other side of the fountain  News Hawker Jason attracts customers. His outcries change depending on the party's recent actions and the outcome of the ⁠Stop the Presses quest.
  • On a sandy patch across the Stormshore Armoury is the cat  Barsik. If the party speak to him via  Speak with Animals, he reveals himself to be a preacher of the goddess  Sharess. If the party agree to hear out the tenets of his "religion", Barsik can be convinced to relieve  Derryth Bonecloak's loneliness if her husband  Baelen did not survive in the Underdark in Act One. If convinced, Barsik runs away and can be later met in the Bonecloak's Apothecary.
  • Behind the building is a greengrocer  Geezer Loryss,[7] ranting about an overturned crate of  Spoiled Cabbage. He is a direct reference to the Cabbage Merchant from Avatar: The Last Airbender animation series, whose cabbage cart was constantly overturned or destroyed by the main protagonist and other characters. If a Monk character talks to Loryss, he has special dialogue lines, also hinting on the series' plot.
  • On a cobbled slope across Loryss's ruined stall lies a free-to-loot backpack with 1 to 3  Thieves' Tools and a  Trap Disarm Toolkit.

Bugs

  • If Rolan is acting as a merchant when the party first enter Sorcerous Sundries, the uniquely named equipment items sold by him remain in his possession, even if Lorroakan's Projection takes over as a merchant after progressing Find the Nightsong, so it will not be possible to get them from Lorroakan's Projection. To get these items, they must be pickpocketed from Rolan or accessed via the Trade option available at the bottom left corner of the screen.
  • Atop the entrance awning of the Sorcerous Sundries is the  Hat of the Sharp Caster hanging in the thin air (as of game version 4.1.1.7151330). This is an item which  Tara used to sell while sitting on the roof of the Devil's Fee. If the party want Tara to progress to her next location, the party must first acquire the hat via Telekinesis or an Arrow of Roaring Thunder, reverse pickpocket it onto her, then buy it back from her, and then take a long rest.
